items.title: Letting Models Manage Their Own Context: Where We Stand
items.snippet: Agent harnesses today manage context on the model's behalf: when the window fills, the harness triggers a compaction that summarizes the history. We study the alternative, model-driven context management, in which the model itself decides when and what to compact through a context API. We gave models control over their own context in \nooa, NVIDIA's open source agent harness, and compared the two strategies on document research and machine learning engineering across context budgets from 8K to 512K tokens. Models that use the context API effectively reach higher accuracy, often with fewer input tokens, especially at tight budgets: GPT 6.1 nearly triples its score at a 32K budget on OfficeQA
items.title_ar: دراسة: تمكين الموديلات من إدارة الـ context بنفسها عبر context API
items.summary_ar: تقارن الورقة بين الـ compaction التي يحركها الـ agent harness وبين إدارة الـ context التي يقررها الموديل نفسه عبر context API. جرى الاختبار داخل nooa، وهو agent harness مفتوح المصدر من NVIDIA، على مهام document research وmachine learning engineering بميزانيات من 8K إلى 512K token. تتفوق الطريقة الثانية في الدقة وغالباً بعدد input tokens أقل، خاصة عند الميزانيات الضيقة.
items.why_ar: تقدم الورقة نمطاً عملياً لإدارة الـ context في agents طويلة وتقييماً مقارنة يفيد أي فريق يبني agents للمستندات.
items.title_en: Letting models manage their own context via a context API
items.summary_en: The paper compares harness-triggered compaction with model-driven context management, where the model decides when and what to compact through a context API. Tests ran in nooa, NVIDIA's open-source agent harness, on document research and ML engineering across 8K to 512K token budgets. The model-driven approach reaches higher accuracy, often with fewer input tokens, especially at tight budgets.
items.why_en: It offers a concrete context-management pattern for long-running agents that document-heavy banking workflows could reuse.

items.title: Lost in Translation, Not in Confidence: Benchmarking and Calibrating Multilingual Decision Models
items.snippet: Decision models are language models fine-tuned to return a probability for each option of a typed query, which routers and guardrails threshold directly. They are built on multilingual bases but ranked almost entirely in English. We evaluate 25 top-ranked open-weight decision models on 17 tasks in 14 languages, comparing each language with English on parallel items. Every model loses accuracy in every language, from about 2 points in high-resource languages to 8 in Tamil, while confidence falls only half as much: a threshold set for 95\% accuracy in English yields 90% in Tamil. The size of the loss is set by the language and the base model rather than by leaderboard rank. In 81 controlled fi
items.title_ar: Decision Models متعددة اللغات: فقدان الدقة وضبط الثقة
items.summary_ar: تقيّم الورقة 25 decision model مفتوحة الأوزان على 17 مهمة بـ 14 لغة، وتقارن كل لغة بالإنجليزية على عناصر متوازية. تجد أن كل موديل يفقد دقة في كل لغة، من نحو 2 نقطة في اللغات عالية الموارد إلى 8 نقاط في Tamil، بينما تنخفض الثقة إلى نصف هذا الفقد تقريباً. وهذا يعني أن عتبة مضبوطة لـ 95% دقة بالإنجليزية تعطي 90% في Tamil.
items.why_ar: يهم هذا المهندس لأن decision models تُستخدم في routers وguardrails، وفقدان الدقة متعدد اللغات يؤثر مباشرة على حلول تعمل بالعربية.
items.title_en: Multilingual Decision Models Lose Accuracy but Not Confidence
items.summary_en: The paper benchmarks 25 top open-weight decision models on 17 tasks across 14 languages, comparing each language with English on parallel items. Every model loses accuracy in every language, up to 8 points in Tamil, while confidence falls only about half as much. A threshold tuned for 95 percent English accuracy yields 90 percent in Tamil.
items.why_en: It directly affects Arabic routing and guardrail thresholds, since miscalibrated confidence across languages can misfire in production.

items.title: Demystifying the Autoresearch Harness: How Context and Skills Shape Self-Evolving Agents
items.snippet: Autoresearch agents, which autonomously design, run, and refine experiments, are accelerating scientific progress, particularly in AI research. However, existing agents rely on harnesses that combine multiple mechanisms, making it difficult to determine how individual components contribute to performance. We systematically study harness design for long-horizon, self-evolving autoresearch agents along two dimensions: context management, which determines what an agent retains from its past attempts, and skill management, which governs how it stores and reuses lessons from those attempts. Across MLE-Bench and KernelBench with gpt-oss-120b, gpt-6-luna, and gpt-6-sol, we isolate the effects of in
items.title_ar: دراسة منهجية لتأثير context وskills في self-evolving agents للبحث الآلي
items.summary_ar: تدرس الورقة تصميم harness لوكلاء autoresearch، وهي وكلاء تصمم التجارب وتشغلها وتحسنها تلقائياً. تفصل الدراسة أثر إدارة السياق، أي ما يحتفظ به الوكيل من محاولاته السابقة، عن إدارة المهارات، أي كيف يخزن الدروس ويعيد استخدامها. تُجرى التجارب على MLE-Bench وKernelBench مع موديلات gpt-oss-120b وgpt-6-luna وgpt-6-sol.
items.why_ar: يهم لأن فهم مكونات harness يساعد في تصميم agents داخلية لتشغيل تجارب POC بكفاءة.
items.title_en: Demystifying the Autoresearch Harness: How Context and Skills Shape Self-Evolving Agents
items.summary_en: The paper systematically studies harness design for self-evolving autoresearch agents that design, run, and refine experiments. It separates the effect of context management, meaning what the agent retains from past attempts, from skill management, meaning how it stores and reuses lessons. Experiments run on MLE-Bench and KernelBench with gpt-oss-120b, gpt-6-luna, and gpt-6-sol.
items.why_en: It clarifies which harness components actually drive agent performance, useful when designing your own experiment-running agents.

items.title: When Every Rollout Fails: Splicing Learner-Conditioned Options into Long-Horizon Agent RL
items.snippet: Group-based reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards often yields all-fail groups on long-horizon agent tasks: every sampled trajectory receives zero reward, leaving group-relative methods without a reward-based policy gradient. A common remedy supplies complete solutions from a stronger model, but full trajectories are expensive and expose the learner to long off-policy histories. We introduce SPLICE, which constructs local training targets from failed current-policy trajectories online. For each all-fail group, a proposal model selects a splice point in a current-policy trajectory and generates several bounded options from that point. We estimate each option's value using repeated cu
items.title_ar: SPLICE: حقن خيارات من learner في RL لـ agents ذات الأفق الطويل
items.summary_ar: تعالج الورقة مشكلة all-fail groups في group-based RL مع verifiable rewards عندما تفشل كل المسارات في مهام agents الطويلة. تقترح SPLICE بناء أهداف تدريب محلية من مسارات فاشلة للسياسة الحالية، عبر اختيار نقطة splice وتوليد options محدودة منها ثم تقدير قيمتها.
items.why_ar: تقدم الورقة تقنية تدريب قابلة للتطبيق لتحسين agents عندما تفشل المحاولات، وهي مفيدة لمن يعمل على تدريب agents.
items.title_en: SPLICE: splicing learner-conditioned options into long-horizon agent RL
items.summary_en: The paper addresses all-fail groups in group-based RL with verifiable rewards, where every sampled trajectory on long-horizon agent tasks gets zero reward. SPLICE builds local training targets online from failed current-policy trajectories by choosing a splice point and generating bounded options from it. Each option's value is then estimated through repeated rollouts.
items.why_en: It proposes a training technique for agents that stall on hard long-horizon tasks, relevant if your team fine-tunes agents with RL.

items.title: Collect for Coverage, Replay with Evidence: Adaptive and Efficient On-Policy Distillation for Long-Horizon Agents
items.snippet: Fully online on-policy distillation (OPD) is costly for long-horizon agents because each update depends on fresh environment rollouts. Prefix replay offers an efficient alternative by sampling current-student responses from stored histories, reducing idle time for long-tail rollouts and allowing each collected trajectory to support multiple updates. However, our analysis of the complete prefix replay pipeline identifies two limitations in long-horizon settings. In trajectory collection, teacher-only trajectories miss student-induced histories, while broader history coverage can reduce teacher reliability. In trajectory reuse, fixed position-based schedules cannot identify critical decisions
items.title_ar: On-Policy Distillation بإعادة تشغيل المسارات المخزنة للوكلاء طويلي المهام
items.summary_ar: تقدم الورقة Prefix Replay كبديل أكفأ لـ on-policy distillation في الوكلاء ذوي المهام الطويلة، إذ تعيد استخدام المسارات المخزنة بدلاً من جمع rollouts جديدة باستمرار. وتحدد الورقة قيدين في خط الأنابيب: أن المسارات التي يولدها teacher وحده تغفل الحالات التي يخلقها student، وأن الجداول الثابتة المعتمدة على الموضع لا تميز القرارات الحرجة. ويقترح الفريق معالجة هذين القيدين بطريقة تكيفية.
items.why_ar: يهم هذا المهندس لأن تدريب agents ذات المهام الطويلة مكلف، وتقليل الحاجة إلى rollouts جديدة يخفض تكلفة التجارب والـ inference.
items.title_en: On-Policy Distillation via Prefix Replay for Long-Horizon Agents
items.summary_en: The paper proposes Prefix Replay as a more efficient alternative to fully online on-policy distillation for long-horizon agents, reusing stored histories instead of fresh rollouts. It identifies two limitations: teacher-only trajectories miss student-induced histories, and fixed position-based replay schedules fail to identify critical decisions. The authors propose an adaptive approach to address both issues.
items.why_en: It matters for agent training costs, since reducing dependence on fresh environment rollouts lowers experiment expenses.

items.title: Evaluation-Free Recursive Self-Improvement for Coding Agents
items.snippet: Recent self-improving coding agents have achieved strong benchmark performance by iteratively modifying their own executable implementations. A common pattern uses downstream task-derived evidence to decide which candidates or lineages continue evolving, which we term evaluate-and-select. Obtaining this signal requires repeatedly executing evolved agents on downstream tasks, so broader exploration incurs increasing evaluation cost, while repeated optimization against a fixed evaluation distribution may encourage benchmark-specific adaptation. We ask: can coding agents self-improve without downstream task evaluation inside the evolution loop? We introduce Explore-then-Integrate (ELITE), which
items.title_ar: تحسين ذاتي متكرر لـ coding agents دون evaluation داخل الحلقة
items.summary_ar: تقدم الورقة Explore-then-Integrate (ELITE) وهي طريقة تسأل إن كان بإمكان coding agents تحسين أنفسهم دون تقييم المهام اللاحقة داخل حلقة التطوير. الدافع أن نمط evaluate-and-select مكلف ومعرض للتكيف مع benchmark محدد. تطرح الورقة بديلاً يعتمد على الاستكشاف ثم الدمج.
items.why_ar: يقترح بديلاً أقل تكلفة لتطوير coding agents دون overfitting على benchmark معين.
items.title_en: Evaluation-Free Recursive Self-Improvement for Coding Agents
items.summary_en: The paper introduces Explore-then-Integrate (ELITE), a method asking whether coding agents can self-improve without downstream task evaluation inside the evolution loop. It motivates this by the cost of evaluate-and-select and the risk of benchmark-specific adaptation. The approach replaces evaluation-driven selection with exploration followed by integration.
items.why_en: It offers a cheaper self-improvement loop for coding agents without benchmark-specific overfitting.

items.title: erkamyaman/safe-anything
items.snippet: Find the holes before someone else does. A fast, 100% Rust vulnerability scanner: XSS, SQL injection, leaked secrets, dependency CVEs and AI agent setups.
items.title_ar: safe-anything: ماسح ثغرات سريع مكتوب بـ Rust يشمل إعدادات AI agents
items.summary_ar: ريبو أداة مفتوحة لفحص الثغرات مكتوبة بالكامل بـ Rust، تكشف XSS وSQL injection والأسرار المسربة وCVEs في dependencies وإعدادات AI agents. تركز على السرعة لاكتشاف الثغرات قبل غيرها.
items.why_ar: يفيد في فحص أمني سريع لمشاريع agents وdependencies قبل نشرها في بيئة بنكية.
items.title_en: safe-anything: Fast Rust Vulnerability Scanner Including AI Agent Setups
items.summary_en: An open tool written entirely in Rust that scans for XSS, SQL injection, leaked secrets, dependency CVEs, and AI agent setups. It focuses on speed to find vulnerabilities before others do.
items.why_en: It can quickly scan agent projects and dependencies for security issues before deployment.

items.title: Efficient Video Retrieval Augmented Generation via Token Allocation
items.snippet: Efficient long-video understanding requires identifying relevant evidence while minimizing the tokens processed by vision-language models (VLMs). Existing video retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) methods rely on frame selection and token compression, but overlook how much each additional token is worth. We introduce Lembas, a plug-and-play framework that formulates video RAG as a token allocation problem over frames and subtitles under a shared budget. Our key insight is that the value of a token diminishes within each item and decreases further as similar evidence receives more tokens. items.title_ar: Lembas: تخصيص الـ tokens في video RAG تحت ميزانية مشتركة
items.summary_ar: تقترح الورقة Lembas، وهي إطار plug-and-play يصيغ video RAG كمسألة تخصيص tokens بين frames وsubtitles ضمن ميزانية مشتركة. تستند الفكرة إلى أن قيمة الـ token تتناقص داخل العنصر نفسه، وتتناقص أكثر عندما يحصل دليل مشابه على tokens إضافية. وتحل الورقة المسألة بخوارزمية water-filling تكرارية.
items.why_ar: يهم هذا المهندس لأن RAG وتقليل الـ tokens في الـ VLMs مفيدان لبناء حلول استرجاع متعددة الوسائط بتكلفة أقل.
items.title_en: Lembas: Token Allocation for Efficient Video RAG
items.summary_en: Lembas is a plug-and-play framework that formulates video RAG as a token allocation problem over frames and subtitles under a shared budget. Its core insight is that the value of a token diminishes within each item and further when similar evidence receives more tokens. It solves the objective with an iterative water-filling method.
items.why_en: It is relevant to RAG cost control, especially for multimodal retrieval over long documents or recordings.
